raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
A shared parameter can contribute to the backward graph through more than one path. The traced graph reduced each contribution separately and added the results:

```python
grad = reduce_grad(local_grad_0) + reduce_grad(local_grad_1)
```

Eager FSDP adds the local contributions first and runs its post-accumulate reduction once:

```python
grad = reduce_grad(local_grad_0 + local_grad_1)
```

With two contributions and 16 microbatches, this changes as many as 32 repeated reductions into local additions followed by one final reduction.

The graph builders now canonicalize their owned joint graph before extraction or partitioning. Every derived graph therefore sees the same form, while the extraction utility remains non-mutating and needs no extra full-graph snapshot.

The change also extracts reusable FX chain and metadata helpers into `common_utils.py` and reuses them in gradient and weight-gradient accumulation.

Validation: 52 focused tests passed across FSDP collective splitting, gradient accumulation, weight-gradient accumulation, and MTP tuple preprocessing.

nodes.body: Closing this redundant replacement because the original #5092 is already recorded as merged. The reviewed coalescing commit remains in the rebased branch ancestry.

Do we understand why do we have such case in the first place? 
I suppose this is coming from MTP using shared weights? 

I wonder this should addressed in simpleFSDP eager code, instead of writing graph pass as an adhoc fix?
Since there are 2 reduce_grad, does it mean there are also 2 allgather for the shared weight?

> help me understand why we have "repeated FSDP gradient reductions" in the first place. Is this a SimpleFSDP bug for shared weights?
@SherlockNoMad 

Yes, this only appeared with MTP, where we have one extra TransformerBlock and shared weight which gradients must be accumulated.

So this is only MTP perf parity

MTP reuses embeddings and lm_head weights:
```
  # Main prediction
  main_embed = tok_embeddings(main_tokens)
  main_logits = lm_head(main_hidden)

  # MTP prediction
  mtp_embed = tok_embeddings(shifted_tokens)
  mtp_logits = lm_head(mtp_hidden)
```
then for gradients 
```
  lm_head_grad =  grad_from_main_loss  + grad_from_mtp_loss
 ```

> Since there are 2 reduce_grad, does it mean there are also 2 allgather for the shared weight?

Yes, there are 2 all-gathers, one of them is redundant. But Sanket already fixed this in https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4934
Some of the helpers in this file seem to overlap with find_fsdp_reduce_grad_input, can we re-use or extend that for this case as well?

help me understand why we have "repeated FSDP gradient reductions" in the first place. 
Is this a SimpleFSDP bug for shared weights?
Yes, thanks, have not noticed them, will extract all reusable methods in common_utils.py and reuse them from there too.

+def _coalesce_fsdp_reduce_grad_add(
+    graph: fx.Graph,
+    grad_outputs: tuple[object, ...],
+) -> None:
+    """Move an add after matching reduce-grad chains before one chain.
+
+    Example::
+
+        local_grad_0 = x @ weight_0                           # not matched
+        local_grad_1 = x @ weight_1                           # not matched
+        reduced_0 = reduce_scatter_tensor(local_grad_0, ...)  # match chain
+        reduced_1 = reduce_scatter_tensor(local_grad_1, ...)  # match chain
+        grad_0 = wait_tensor(reduced_0)                       # match chain
+        grad_1 = wait_tensor(reduced_1)                       # match chain
+        output = grad_0 + grad_1                              # match add
+        consumer = output.view(-1)                            # not matched
+
+    Output::
+        combined = local_grad_0 + local_grad_1
+        reduced = reduce_scatter_tensor(combined, ...)
+        output = wait_tensor(reduced)
+        consumer = output.view(-1)
+    """
+    current_grad_outputs = list(grad_outputs)
+    while True:
+        changed = False
+        node_order = {node: index for index, node in enumerate(graph.nodes)}
+        adds = tuple(
+            candidate
+            for grad_output in current_grad_outputs
+            for candidate in _gradient_add_candidates(grad_output)
+        )
+        for add, param_fqns in adds:
+            if not isinstance(param_fqns, tuple) or len(param_fqns) != 1:
+                continue
+            lhs, rhs = add.args[:2]
+            if (
+                not isinstance(lhs, fx.Node)
+                or not isinstance(rhs, fx.Node)
+                or lhs is rhs
+            ):
+                continue
+            lhs_chain = find_fsdp_unary_reduce_grad_chain(lhs)
+            rhs_chain = find_fsdp_unary_reduce_grad_chain(rhs)
+            if lhs_chain is None or rhs_chain is None:
+                continue
+            lhs_boundary, lhs_nodes = lhs_chain
+            rhs_boundary, rhs_nodes = rhs_chain
+            if not _matching_reduce_grad_chains(
+                lhs_boundary,
+                lhs_nodes,
+                rhs_boundary,
+                rhs_nodes,
+                param_fqns,
+                add,
+            ):
+                continue
+            if not chain_has_exclusive_users(
+                lhs_nodes, add
+            ) or not chain_has_exclusive_users(rhs_nodes, add):
+                continue
+
+            if node_order[lhs_boundary] < node_order[rhs_boundary]:
+                kept_output, kept_boundary, kept_nodes = (
+                    rhs,
+                    rhs_boundary,
+                    rhs_nodes,
+                )
+                dropped_nodes = lhs_nodes
+            else:
+                kept_output, kept_boundary, kept_nodes = (
+                    lhs,
+                    lhs_boundary,
+                    lhs_nodes,
+                )
+                dropped_nodes = rhs_nodes
+
+            # The later boundary is after both local gradients, so inserting
+            # before its chain preserves FX topological order.
+            with graph.inserting_before(kept_nodes[0]):
+                combined = graph.call_function(
+                    torch.ops.aten.add.Tensor,
+                    args=(lhs_boundary, rhs_boundary),
+                )
+            combined.meta = copy(lhs_boundary.meta)
+            combined.meta["custom"] = copy(combined.meta.get("custom", {}))
+            combined.meta["custom"][PARAMETER_GRADIENT_FQNS_META] = param_fqns
+            kept_nodes[0].replace_input_with(kept_boundary, combined)
+            kept_output.meta.setdefault("custom", {}).update(add.meta.get("custom", {}))
+            add.replace_all_uses_with(kept_output)
+            current_grad_outputs[:] = [
+                kept_output if output is add else output
+                for output in current_grad_outputs
+            ]
+            # Validate the rewired graph before deleting the mutation chain.
+            graph.lint()
+            graph.erase_node(add)
+            for node in reversed(dropped_nodes):
+                assert not node.users
+                graph.erase_node(node)
+            graph.lint()
+            changed = True
+            break
+        if not changed:
+            return
+
+

issue_comments.body: Closing this redundant replacement because the original #5092 is already recorded as merged. The reviewed coalescing commit remains in the rebased branch ancestry.

Do we understand why do we have such case in the first place? 
I suppose this is coming from MTP using shared weights? 

I wonder this should addressed in simpleFSDP eager code, instead of writing graph pass as an adhoc fix?
Since there are 2 reduce_grad, does it mean there are also 2 allgather for the shared weight?

> help me understand why we have "repeated FSDP gradient reductions" in the first place. Is this a SimpleFSDP bug for shared weights?
@SherlockNoMad 

Yes, this only appeared with MTP, where we have one extra TransformerBlock and shared weight which gradients must be accumulated.

So this is only MTP perf parity

MTP reuses embeddings and lm_head weights:
```
  # Main prediction
  main_embed = tok_embeddings(main_tokens)
  main_logits = lm_head(main_hidden)

  # MTP prediction
  mtp_embed = tok_embeddings(shifted_tokens)
  mtp_logits = lm_head(mtp_hidden)
```
then for gradients 
```
  lm_head_grad =  grad_from_main_loss  + grad_from_mtp_loss
 ```

> Since there are 2 reduce_grad, does it mean there are also 2 allgather for the shared weight?

Yes, there are 2 all-gathers, one of them is redundant. But Sanket already fixed this in https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/4934
